subject: psychology
title: Development: Foundations of Piaget
welcome_lead: Step into Piaget's classroom and trace how children build minds stage by stage.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology adventure on cognitive development: Piaget's stages, schemas, assimilation, accommodation and equilibration.
final_note: You have mapped Piaget's blueprint for the growing mind.

concepts.def: A mental framework that organises knowledge about the world.
Fitting new information into an existing schema.
Changing a schema to fit new information.
Balancing assimilation and accommodation to learn.
Piaget's stage 0-2 years: senses, motor actions, object permanence.
Piaget's stage 2-7 years: symbols, egocentrism, no conservation.

walkthroughs.body_html: Piaget proposed four invariant stages: sensorimotor (0-2), preoperational (2-7), concrete operational (7-11) and formal operational (11+). Each stage builds on the last, and all children move through them in the same order.

A child has a schema for 'dog'. Seeing a new dog and adding it to the schema is assimilation. Seeing a cat and creating a new schema is accommodation. The drive to restore balance between the two is equilibration.

walkthroughs.h2: Why young children cannot see other views
walkthroughs.body_html: In the preoperational stage children are egocentric — they assume others see what they see. Piaget's Three Mountains task showed children under 7 picked their own view of the mountains, not the doll's.
